This is a list of national population and housing [[census]]es.
[[File:Most Recent Census Conducted.png|thumb|300px|World map showing countries' most recent censuses as of 2025]]

== Census advisory ==
The United Nations recommends a census enumeration at least once every ten years, and once every five years for even better data, rather than simply relying on estimates and projections alone.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://unstats.un.org/unsd/publication/seriesm/seriesm_67rev2e.pdf |title=Principles and Recommendations for Population and Housing Censuses Revision 2}}</ref> Complications to carrying out a census include tribal conflict, war, borders not demarcated, budget, inexperience, political snags, lack of manpower, and poor [[geographic information system]]s.  A number of nations have not carried them out once a decade. It is not uncommon for a scheduled census to be deferred or delayed.

Lebanon has not held a census since 1932.  Afghanistan is closing in on five decades without a census. DRC and Uzbekistan stand out as not having a census since before 1990. Eritrea has only had one as a part of Ethiopia in the 1990s.

==Methods of conducting population census==
More countries are switching to using administrative data to hold a census. This allows a simulated census to be conducted by linking several different administrative databases at an agreed time.

==Africa==
===Algeria===
Population and housing censuses have been carried out in [[Algeria]] in 1966, 1977, 1987, 1998,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ons.dz/-Population-.html|title=Population|publisher=National Statistical Office (Algeria)|access-date=18 May 2019}}</ref> 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ons.dz/collections/|title=Résultats Du Recensement Général De La Population et De L'Habitat 2008|publisher=National Statistical Office (Algeria)|access-date=18 May 2019}}</ref> and 2020.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Historical |url=https://www.ons.dz/rgph2020/language/fr/historique/ |access-date=8 August 2025 |website=PEOPLE'S DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF ALGERIA National Statistics Office GENERAL POPULATION AND HOUSING CENSUS 2020}}</ref>

===Angola===
{{further|Angola}}

General censuses of population and housing ([[Portuguese language|Portuguese]]: ''Recenseamento Geral da População e Habitação'' (RGPH)) were carried out in 1970 and 2014. The 1970 census counted 5,646,166 habitants. The 2014 census counted 25,789,024 habitants as of May 16, 2014.<ref name=unpop>{{cite web | url=https://www.embajadadeangola.com/pdf/Publicacao%20Resultados%20Definitivos%20Censo%20Geral%202014_Versao%2022032016_DEFINITIVA%2018H17.pdf | title=''Resultados definitivos do recenseamento geral – 2014'' | publisher=Instituto Nacional de Estatística (INE) | access-date=2019-12-23}}</ref>

===Benin===
Population and housing censuses have been carried out in 1978, [[1992 Benin census|1992]], 2002 and 2013.<ref name=OrissaReview2010 /><ref name="insae-bj.org">{{cite web|url=https://www.insae-bj.org/recensement-population.html|title=Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitation – INSAE|website=www.insae-bj.org}}</ref> 2013 census preliminary results have been published.<ref name="insae-bj.org"/> Final results were published in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.beninsite.net/spip.php?article15785 |title=Investissements publics et les mesures prioritaires du Gouvernement :3 milliards pour promouvoir la culture béninoise en 2015 – 1er Portail Béninois d'Informations |access-date=December 4, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141115181230/http://www.beninsite.net/spip.php?article15785 |archive-date=November 15, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Botswana===
{{Main|Census in Botswana}}

Censuses in [[Botswana]] are run by the [[Statistics Botswana]] (formerly Central Statistics Office). There have been twelve censuses in Botswana's history. The most recent occurred in April 2022.

===Burkina Faso===
The Institut National de la Statistique et de la Demographie has conducted four censuses: in 1975, 1985, 1996, 2006 and 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insd.bf/n/nada/index.php/catalog/RGPH|title=Catalogue de données central › Recensement Généraux de la Population et de l'Habitat|publisher=Institut National de la Statistique et de la Demographie (Burkina Faso)|access-date=21 May 2019|archive-date=May 16, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190516214221/http://www.insd.bf/n/nada/index.php/catalog/RGPH|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Congo (DRC)===
The first and so far only census conducted in DR Congo dates from 1984.<ref>[https://ireda.ceped.org/inventaire/ressources/cod-1984-rec-o1_resultats_provisoires.pdf Recensement scientifique de la population 1984. Résultats provisoires]</ref>

===Egypt===
{{Main|Census in Egypt}}

The Statistical Department of the Ministry of Finance conducted the first census in 1882, which considered as a preparatory step; the first true population census was conducted in 1897. Thereafter, censuses were conducted at ten-year intervals in 1907, 1917, 1927 and so on. The last one being in 2017.

===Ethiopia===
Three censuses have been taken in [[Ethiopia]]: 1984, 1994 and in 2007. The responsible institution is the [[Central Statistical Agency (Ethiopia)|Central Statistical Agency]]. Most of the census in 2007 was taken in August, while the [[Somali Region]] and the [[Afar Region]] were not covered. The northern Afar region is a remote, hot and arid area. The eastern Somali region ([[Ogaden]]) hosts a large nomadic Somali population and is a conflict area where Ethiopian regular forces are fighting against [[Ogaden National Liberation Front]] ([[ONLF]]).<ref name=OrissaReview2010 />

===Ivory Coast===
{{Main|Demographics of Ivory Coast}}

===Kenya===
The first census in [[Kenya]] was conducted in 1948, when Kenya was still a colony administered by the British. Since 1969 census has been taken every ten years. The last census, overseen by the [[Kenya National Bureau of Statistics]], was in 2019 and recorded a population of 47.6&nbsp;million.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.knbs.or.ke/?p=5621|title=2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census Results|date=November 4, 2019}}</ref>

===Madagascar===
Madagascar had its latest census in 2018, the third census to be conducted. It recorded a total resident population of 25,674,186 inhabitants.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.instat.mg/p/resultats-definitifs-du-rgph-3-2018-troisieme-recensement-general-de-la-population-et-de-lhabitation |title=Résultats définitifs du RGPH-3 2018 {{!}} Troisième Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitation |date=May 4, 2021 |website=INSTAT |language=fr |access-date=March 16, 2025}}</ref>

===Mauritius===
Population and housing censuses for [[Mauritius]] was collected in 1972, 1983, 2000, and 2011; although respondents were asked to identify their race/ethnic origin in the 1972 census, this question was dropped from the following censuses because "the government felt that it was a divisive question".<ref>[http://www.statssa.gov.za/asc/WebsiteReports/Mauritius.pdf "2010 Round of Censuses: Learning from the 2000 Round Country position: Mauritius February 2006"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070610142505/http://www.statssa.gov.za/asc/WebsiteReports/Mauritius.pdf |date=June 10, 2007 }}. Retrieved April 3, 2009.</ref> The Statistics Act directed that all official censuses be conducted by [[Statistics Mauritius]], as well as serve as the central depository for this information.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gov.mu/portal/site/cso/menuitem.922af73ab9a84a9e965c062ca0208a0c/|title=Central Statistics Office: The Statistics Act 2000|access-date=November 14, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120821135643/http://www.gov.mu/portal/site/cso/menuitem.922af73ab9a84a9e965c062ca0208a0c/|archive-date=August 21, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Morocco===
{{main|Moroccan census}}

General censuses of population and housing (Arabic: الإحصاء العام للسكان والسكنى / French: ''Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat'' (RGPH)) have been carried out since independence in 1960, 1971, 1982, 1994, 2004 and 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://rgph-2014.hcp.ma/Apercu-sur-les-recensements-au-Maroc_a29.html|title=Aperçu sur les recensements au Maroc|first=Sobha|last=Sobhaz}}</ref> The 2014 census results will be published on <nowiki>http://rgph-2014.hcp.ma/</nowiki> by the end of 2014.

===Mozambique===
The first census was taken in 1980. The second in 1997. The third was taken August 1–14, 2007. The fourth and most recent was taken in 2017.

===Namibia===
In accordance with the ''Statistics Act No. 66 of 1976'', [[Namibia]] conducts a Population and Housing Census every ten years. After [[Independence of Namibia|independence]] the first one was carried out in 1991, further rounds followed in 2001 and 2011.<ref name=2001Census>{{cite web
 |url         = http://www.npc.gov.na/census/index.htm
 |title       = Census Summary Results
 |publisher   = National Planning Commission of Namibia
 |access-date  = February 21, 2012
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120111224420/http://www.npc.gov.na/census/index.htm
 |archive-date = January 11, 2012
 |df          = mdy-all
}}</ref> In Namibia, the ''de facto'' method is used.<ref>{{cite news
|url=http://allafrica.com/stories/201108080754.html
|title=Namibia: 2011 Census Officially Launched
|last=Kapitako
|first=Alvine
|date=August 8, 2011
|work=[[New Era (Namibia)|New Era]]
|publisher=via allafrica.com}}</ref> For enumeration purposes the country is demarcated into 4,042 ''enumeration areas''. These areas do not overlap with constituency boundaries to get reliable data for election purposes as well.<ref>{{cite web
 |url         = http://www.npc.gov.na/census/index.htm
 |title       = Methodology
 |publisher   = National Planning Commission of Namibia
 |access-date  = February 21, 2012
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120111224420/http://www.npc.gov.na/census/index.htm
 |archive-date = January 11, 2012
 |df          = mdy-all
}}</ref>

===Nigeria===
Population censuses have been taken in [[Nigeria]] during colonial time in 1866, 1871, 1896, 1901, 1911, 1921 and 1952. The censuses covered only the southern part of the country except for the 1952 census which was country wide, and the censuses before 1921 were based on administrative estimates rather than on an actual enumeration.

Censuses during independence were taken 1962, 1963, 1973, 1991 and 2006. The results of the 1962 census were considered inaccurate enough that a new census was ordered on February 19, 1963.<ref>Larry Diamond, ''Class, Ethnicity, and Democracy in Nigeria: The Failure of the First Republic'' (Syracuse University Press, 1988) p136</ref> The results from 1973 and 2006 were highly disputed, but no recounts were taken. The preliminary results for 2006 indicates a population of 140&nbsp;million people. 700,000 enumerators were engaged in this operation.

===Somalia===
There has been only one successful census in [[Somalia]], carried out in 1975. The 1986 census remained incomplete, and its results were never published.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nbs.gov.so/volume-1-methodology-and-assessment-of-data-quality-of-the-somali-people/|title=Somali National Bureau of Statistics|website=www.nbs.gov.so |date=December 5, 2014 }}</ref>

===South Africa===
The Cape of Good Hope conducted the first modern scientific census in 1865, following the principles laid down by the British Colonial Office and repeated the exercise in 1875 and 1891.23 The Orange Free State followed in 1880 and 1890, copying many of the features of the Cape of Good Hope.24 The South African Republic (Transvaal) followed in 1890.However, the enumeration was restricted to the White population. 
After the South African War of 1899–1902, all the colonies undertook censuses in April 1904, but although broad coordination took place the results were presented according to the views of the four individual census commissioners.28 The detailed coordination of censuses evident in pre-federation Australia was therefore not in evidence in South Africa.
The establishment of the Union of South Africa as a British dominion in 1910 necessitated a new start to enumeration in the country and the statistical definition of the new state and ordering of its population through the census.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Christopher |first1=A. J. |title=The Union of South Africa censuses 1911-1960: an incomplete record |journal=Historia |date=November 2011 |volume=56 |issue=2 |pages=1–18 |url=http://www.scielo.org.za/scielo.php?pid=S0018-229X2011000200001&script=sci_abstract }}</ref>
<ref>G20-'66, Census of the Colony of the Cape of Good Hope 1865 (Government Printer, Cape Town, 1866); G42-'76, Census of the Colony of the Cape of Good Hope 1875, Part I Summaries (Government Printer, Cape Town, 1877); G6-'92, Census of the Colony of the Cape of Good Hope 1891 (Government Printer, Cape Town, 1892)</ref>
The first census of Union of South Africa was taken in 1911. Several enumerations have occurred since then,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://countrystudies.us/south-africa/44.htm|title=South Africa – Population|website=countrystudies.us}}</ref> with the most recent three being carried out by [[Statistics South Africa]] in 1996, [[South African National Census of 2001|2001]], [[South African National Census of 2011|2011]] and 2022.

===Sudan===
Population censuses have been carried out in [[Sudan]] in 1955/56, 1973 (national), 1983 (national) and 1993 (only north). A census was conducted in April 2008. Some areas—namely [[Darfur]], [[Juba]], and [[Malakal]]—were difficult to measure.{{citation needed|date=November 2023}}

===Togo===
General population and housing censuses were carried out in 1960, 1970, 1981 and 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stat-togo.org/index.php?option=com_docman&task=doc_download&gid=131&&Itemid=56 |title=Institut National de la Statistique et des Etudes Économiques et Démographiques |website=www.stat-togo.org |access-date=6 June 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210930145750/http://www.stat-togo.org/index.php?option=com_docman&task=doc_download&gid=131&&Itemid=56 |archive-date=30 September 2021 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Tunisia===
General censuses of population and housing (French: ''Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat'' (RGPH)) have been carried out in 1921, 1926, 1931, 1936, 1946, 1956, 1966, 1975, 1984, 1994, 2004 and 2014.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.slideshare.net/fullscreen/kimo0147/dpliant-39093576/1 |title=Dépliant premiers résultats du Recensement de la population et de |access-date=November 26, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141217004349/http://www.slideshare.net/fullscreen/kimo0147/dpliant-39093576/1 |archive-date=December 17, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> First results<ref>{{cite web |url=http://rgph2014.ins.tn/fr/resultats |title=Resultats &#124; Institut National des Statistiques |access-date=2014-11-26 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029170649/http://rgph2014.ins.tn/fr/resultats |archive-date=October 29, 2014 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> (20%) were published on September 12, 2014,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://rgph2014.ins.tn/fr/premiers-r%C3%A9sultats-du-recensement-2014 |title=Premiers résultats du Recensement 2014 &#124; Institut National des Statistiques |access-date=November 26, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141204201537/http://rgph2014.ins.tn/fr/premiers-r%C3%A9sultats-du-recensement-2014 |archive-date=December 4, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> the final results were published between January and December 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://rgph2014.ins.tn/fr/calendrier |title=Calendrier &#124; Institut National des Statistiques |access-date=November 26, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141029191234/http://rgph2014.ins.tn/fr/calendrier |archive-date=October 29, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Uganda===
{{Main|Uganda Bureau of Statistics}}

The first censuses in [[Uganda]] were taken in 1911, 1921 and 1931. It was done in a rather primitive way. The [[enumeration]] unit was 'huts' and not individuals. More scientific censuses were taken 1948 and 1959 where the enumeration unit was persons. The census was however divided into two separate enumerations, one for Africans, and one for the non-African population.

The censuses during independence 1969, 1980, 1991 were taken jointly for all races. The censuses 1980 and 1991 included housing information and in addition a larger questionnaire for a sample of the population. However, the questionnaires for the 1980 were lost and only provisional figures are available from this census.

The census in 2002 involved some 50,000 enumerators and supervisors. It covered several topics including: population and housing; agriculture; and Micro- and small Enterprises administered at individual/household level. The Preliminary Results were published two weeks after the enumeration. The Final Results were released in March 2005, while the analytical findings and the district level results were scheduled to be released in the second quarter of 2006.<ref>[http://www.statssa.gov.za/asc/WebsiteReports/Uganda.pdf "Country submission for Uganda: The 2010 World Programme on Population and Housing Censuses"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070610142625/http://www.statssa.gov.za/asc/WebsiteReports/Uganda.pdf |date=June 10, 2007 }}, Africa Symposium on the 2010 Round of Population and Housing Censuses (Cape Town, South Africa), January 30 – February 2, 2006. Retrieved April 3, 2009.</ref>

The next census was conducted in August 2014 under the theme of ‘Counting for Planning and Improved Service Delivery’.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ubos.org/2014-census|title=2014 Census – Uganda Bureau of Statistics|website=www.ubos.org}}</ref> Provisional results were released in November 2014 and the main report was released in March 2016.<ref>Uganda Bureau of Statistics (2016). ''The National Population and Housing Census 2014: Final Results, Main Report''. Kampala: Uganda Bureau of Statistics. Available at: https://uganda.unfpa.org/sites/default/files/pub-pdf/CENSUS%202014%20Final%20Results_0.pdf (accessed 10 October 2025).</ref> In August 2024, the latest census was conducted under the theme of 'It matters to be counted'. The final report was released in December 2024.<ref>Uganda Bureau of Statistics (2025). ''National Population and Housing Census 2024: Final Report, Volume I — Main Report''. Kampala: Uganda Bureau of Statistics. Available at: https://statistics.ubos.org/nphc/reports/National-Population-and-Housing-Census-2024-Final-Report-Volume-1-Main.pdf (accessed 10 October 2025).</ref>

=== Barbados ===
Censuses on population sizes in Barbados are conducted by the Barbados Statistical Service (BSS). The last major census was conducted in 2021.

=== Bolivia ===
{{Main|National Institute of Statistics of Bolivia}}

[[File:Bolivia in South America.svg|thumb|right|Map of Bolivia in the Americas]]
Bolivia became independent from Spain on August 6, 1825, and since that time the country has managed to carry out around 11 population and housing censuses throughout its history as an independent country.

The first population census of Bolivia was carried out in 1831 and four years later the second census was carried out in 1835, the third in 1845, the fourth in 1854 and finally the fifth census was in 1882, this being the last 19th century census.

During the 20th century, Bolivia only carried out four censuses; the first at the beginning of the century in 1900 and the second census was in 1950 (after 50 years) already in the middle of the 20th century. The next census was carried out 26 years later in 1976 and the next census was carried out after 16 years in 1992, this being also the last of the century.

At the beginning of the 21st century, Bolivia carried out a new population census in 2001 and after 11 years the next census was carried out again in 2012. Currently and after 12 years, Bolivia will carry out its third census on March 23, 2024, this being the third population and housing census of the century

=== Brazil ===
{{Further|Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics}}The Brazilian census is carried out by the [[Brazilian Institute of Geography and Statistics]] every [[decennial|10 years]]. The last one was in 2010. Earlier censuses were taken in 1872 ([[1872 Brazilian Census|the first]]), 1900, 1920, 1941, 1950, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1991, 2000 and 2010.

Brazil's Demographic Census is one of the most [[hierarchical]] collection of census data in the world. Its hierarchies include: Brazil (Country), Major Regions, States, Macro-regions, micro-regions, municipalities, districts, sub-districts, Neighborhoods and census tracts.

Depending on the administrative hierarchy, some types of data are not published to respect confidentiality.

For example:
#The lower area of data collection is the census tract, with approximately 300 households, and information is collected on age, condition of the home, gender, income, among others.
#Districts: information on race, color, religion, disability, etc.
#Municipalities (cities): in addition to the information already described, there is information of GDP, industrial production, agricultural production, migration between cities to study or work, to live migration, inflation, employment rates, number of industries, the quantity of trade, etc.
Information is collected with [[:pt:Ficheiro:Ibge em poá são paulo brasil.jpg|handheld computers]] equipped with GPS receivers and digitized maps.

Next census was scheduled to begin August 1, 2020 but was delayed two times due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-03-17|title=Censo 2020 adiado para 2021 |url=https://www.ibge.gov.br/novo-portal-destaques/27161-censo-2020-adiado-para-2021.html|access-date=2022-01-23|website=IBGE|language=PT-BR}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-04-23|title=Adiamento do Censo Demográfico |url=https://www.ibge.gov.br/novo-portal-destaques/30569-adiamento-do-censo-demografico.html|access-date=2022-01-23|website=IBGE|language=PT-BR}}</ref> The Census is scheduled to begin on August 1, 2022. More than one million people applied for 206.891 positions.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-23|title=Concurso do Censo 2022 tem mais de 1,1 milhão de inscritos para 206,8 mil vagas|url=https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/business/concurso-do-censo-2022-tem-mais-de-11-milhao-para-2068-mil-vagas/|access-date=2022-01-23|website=CNN Brasil|language=pt-BR}}</ref>

=== Canada ===
{{Main|Census in Canada}}

The Canadian census is run by [[Statistics Canada]]. The [[1666 census of New France]] was conducted by French [[intendant of New France|intendant]] [[Jean Talon]], when he took a census to ascertain the number of people living in [[New France]]. The method and data was later used when Canada was founded 201 years later. The individual provinces (sometimes in conjunction with each other) conducted censuses in the 19th century and before. In 1871, Canada's first formal census was conducted, which counted the population of [[Nova Scotia]], Ontario, [[New Brunswick]], and [[Quebec]].

Censuses in Canada are conducted in five-year intervals. The last census was conducted in 2021. Censuses taken in mid-decade (1976, 1986, 1996, etc.) are referred to as quinquennial censuses. Others are referred to as decennial censuses. The first quinquennial census was conducted in 1956.

For the 2006 Census of Canada, respondents were able to complete their census questionnaire online for the first time. Other options for answering the questionnaire included postal mail (using a pre-paid envelope) and telephone (using an [[Toll-free telephone number|800 number]]).

At a sub-national level, two provinces ([[Alberta]] and [[Saskatchewan]]) and two territories ([[Nunavut]] and [[Yukon]]) have legislation that allows local governments to conduct their own [[Municipal census in Canada|municipal censuses]].<ref name=municipalcensus>{{cite web | url=https://webdocs.edmonton.ca/OcctopusDocs/Public/Complete/Reports/CC/Elected-1995/2006-07-18/2006CMC047.doc | title=Municipal Census Policy (City Council Agenda Item No. E.1.l) | publisher=City of Edmonton | type=[[Doc (computing)|DOC]] | date=May 31, 2006 | access-date=December 24, 2013}}</ref>

=== Chile ===
National population censuses are carried out in Chile every ten years by the [[National Statistics Institute (Chile)|National Statistics Institute]] (INE). The last one took place in 2012, but its results were dismissed by the INE due to a high omission rate and other problems.<ref>{{cite web|last1=s. a. p. |first1=El Mercurio |url=https://www.lasegunda.com/Noticias/Economia/2014/09/964466/ine-concluye-que-datos-del-mejor-censo-de-la-historia-de-chile-no-sirven-para-nada|title=INE concluye que datos del "mejor censo de la historia de Chile" no sirven para nada|work=El Mercurio}}</ref> A new abbreviated census took place in April 2017, with a full census to be carried out in 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.emol.com/noticias/economia/2014/11/24/691415/directora-del-ine-se-reune-por-primera-vez-con-comite-asesor-externo-del-censo-abreviado-2017.html|title=Directora del INE se reúne por primera vez con Comité Asesor Externo del Censo Abreviado 2017|work=El Mercurio|date=November 24, 2014}}</ref> The last official census results are from 2002.

=== Costa Rica ===
Costa Rica carried out its [[Costa Rica 2011 Census|tenth population census]] in 2011. [[National Institute of Statistics and Census of Costa Rica|INEC]], ''National Institute of Statistics and Census'' is in charge of conduct these censuses. Past Costa Rican censuses were conducted in 1864, 1883, 1892, 1927, 1950, 1963, 1973, 1984, and 2000. The next census is scheduled for 2022.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.inec.cr/censos/censo-2022|title = Censo 2022 |website=Instituto Nacional de Estadistica y Censos}}</ref>

===Cuba===
Cuba carried out its [[2012 Cuba census|eighteenth population census]] in 2012. The next census is scheduled for 2025.

=== Curaçao ===

General censuses of population and housing have been carried out in 1960, 1971, 1981, 1992, 2001, and 2011. In 2021 a new census will be conducted by the Central Bureau of Statistics of Curaçao. For more information and the results of the older censuses visit the [https://digitallibrary.cbs.cw/ DIgitallibrary of CBS]

=== Guatemala ===
Modern population censuses have been taken in Guatemala in 1930, 1950, 1964, 1973, 1981, 1994, 2002 and 2018.<ref>{{cite web|title=Portal de Resultados del Censo 2018|language=Spanish|url=https://www.censopoblacion.gt/explorador|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200416035709/https://www.censopoblacion.gt/explorador|access-date=2025-04-24|archive-date=2020-04-16}}</ref> Controversial censuses include those in 1950 and 1964 (misclassification of the Maya population) and 1994 (generally questioned). About 14,000,000 people live in Guatemala as of July 2009.

=== Haiti ===
General censuses of population and housing (French: ''Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat'' (RGPH)) have been carried out in 1950, 1971, 1982, 2003 and 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ihsi.ht/produit_enq_nat.htm|title=IHSI – Produits – Enquêtes Nationales|website=www.ihsi.ht}}</ref> First results of the 2014 census will be published between November and December 2014;<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/mefhaiti/docs/documentvergph_2014drv|title=5e Recensement Général de la Population et de l'Habitat (Ve RGPH-2014) by MEF Haiti – Issuu|date=December 16, 2013|website=issuu.com}}</ref> final results will be published in November 2015.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://lenouvelliste.com/lenouvelliste/article/123317/Le-MEF-et-lIHSI-lancent-le-5e-Recensement-general-de-la-population-et-de-lhabitat |title=Le MEF et l'IHSI lancent le 5e Recensement général de la population et de l'habitat |access-date=November 27, 2014 |archive-date=December 5, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141205044432/http://lenouvelliste.com/lenouvelliste/article/123317/Le-MEF-et-lIHSI-lancent-le-5e-Recensement-general-de-la-population-et-de-lhabitat |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Honduras===
[[Honduras]] has held a national census every 11–14 years since 1950. Its first census as an independent country took place in 1881. The next census is scheduled to be held in 2026.

=== Mexico ===
{{main|Censo General de Población y Vivienda}}

* National population censuses have been carried out in 1910, 1921, 1930, 1940, 1950, 1960, 1970, 1980, 1990, 1995, 2000, 2005 and 2010.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.inegi.org.mx/sistemas/mexicocifras/default.aspx|title=INEGI – México en cifras|date=November 13, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101113142319/http://www.inegi.org.mx/sistemas/mexicocifras/default.aspx|archive-date=November 13, 2010|df=mdy-all }}</ref>
* National economic censuses have been carried out in 1989, 1994, 1999, 2004, 2009 and 2014.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.inegi.org.mx/est/contenidos/Proyectos/ce/Default.aspx|title=Censos Económicos|website=www.inegi.org.mx}}</ref>

=== United States ===
{{Main|United States census|State censuses in the United States}}

The [[United States Constitution]] and federal law mandate that a census be taken every ten years to apportion the number of members of the [[United States House of Representatives]] among the several states.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.census.gov/history/pdf/Article_1_Section_2.pdf |title=Article 1, Section 2 of the United States Constitution|website=census.gov|access-date=26 September 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
|url=https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/13/141|title=13 U.S. Code § 141 – Population and other census information|website=LII / Legal Information Institute}}</ref> Census statistics are also used to apportion federal funding for many social and economic programs.

The first [[United States Census|U.S. Census]] was conducted in 1790 by [[United States Marshals Service|Federal Marshals]]. During the 19th century and through the 1940 census, enumeration was accomplished through political districts. Each [[political ward|ward]] was responsible for producing a census.

From 1950 onward, census forms were mailed to every address on record with the [[United States Post Office]], including the Armed Services Postal System, in an effort to enhance completeness of the data collected. Beginning in 1970, it was made illegal to fail to return a completed census form. Computer technology was also introduced.

The [[2010 United States census|2010 census]] counted over 308 million people.

By law (92 Stat. 915, Public Law 95-416, enacted on October 5, 1978), individual census records are sealed for 72 years.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.census.gov/history/www/reference/legislation/legislation_1974_-_1983.html|title=Legislation 1974 – 1983 – History – U.S. Census Bureau|first=Census History Staff|last=US Census Bureau|website=www.census.gov}}</ref> The individual census data most recently released to the public was the 1940 census, released on April 2, 2012. Aggregate census data are released when available.

In addition to the decennial federal census, local censuses have also been conducted, for example, in [[Massachusetts]], which conducted a statewide census every five years until 1985. Some states conducted limited censuses for various purposes, and these are typically located in state archives.

Next census was scheduled to begin 1 April 2020<ref>[[2020 United States census]]</ref>{{circular reference|date=August 2020}} but delays due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic meant most areas did not assign enumerators and begin counting until after August 1, 2020, even while their questions are still written to tabulate information about a housing unit's status on the prior date.

The [[2020 United States census|2020 census]] counted for over 331 million people.<ref>{{Cite web|title=U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts: United States (V2021)|url=https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/US/PST045221|access-date=2022-01-23|website=Census Bureau|language=en}}</ref>

=== Venezuela ===
The study of the population in Venezuela is in charge of the National Institute of Statistics, which is in charge of collecting, analyzing and publishing data. Its best known publication is the Population Census, which is carried out in a period of no more than 15 years.

The last study of this type was carried out in 2011 between September and November.<ref>{{Cite web|title=INE da a conocer los Primeros Resultados del Censo 2011|url=http://www.ine.gov.ve/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=423:ine-da-a-conocer-los-primeros-resultados-del-censo-2011|access-date=2021-02-25|website=www.ine.gov.ve}}</ref>

==Asia==
===Afghanistan===
A partial and incomplete population census was taken in Afghanistan in June 1979.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://iranicaonline.org/|title=Welcome to Encyclopaedia Iranica|first=Encyclopaedia Iranica|last=Foundation|website=iranicaonline.org}}</ref><ref name=OrissaReview2010>{{cite journal |title=Census in Different Countries of the World |url=http://orissa.gov.in/e-magazine/Orissareview/2010/December/engpdf/26-36.pdf |journal=Orissa Review |date=December 2010 |pages=26 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141206060631/http://orissa.gov.in/e-magazine/Orissareview/2010/December/engpdf/26-36.pdf |archive-date=December 6, 2014}}</ref> Wars since then have caused significant population displacement and there has not been an updated count nor does the nation seem to have the technical ability nor will to tackle a modern census.

===Armenia===
{{main|Census in Armenia}}

Population censuses have been taken in Armenia under Russian/Soviet rule in 1831, 1873, 1886, 1897, 1922, 1926, 1939, 1959, 1970, 1979, and 1989. Beginning in 1991, three more censuses' have been carried out in Armenia: one in 2001, one in 2011 and one in 2022.<ref>[https://armenpress.am/en/article/1110018 Armenia’s permanent population is 2,928,914, according to new census]. ''[[Armenpress]]''. May 2, 2023. Retrieved September 23, 2024.</ref>

===Azerbaijan===
{{main|Census in Azerbaijan}}

Population censuses have been taken in Azerbaijan under Russian/Soviet rule in 1897, 1926, 1937, 1939, 1959, 1970, 1979, and 1989. Beginning in 1991, two more censuses have been carried out in Azerbaijan: one in 1999 and one in 2009.<ref>[https://www.rferl.org/a/Population_Census_Gets_Under_Way_In_Azerbaijan/1608527.html Population Census Gets Under Way In Azerbaijan]. ''Radio Free Europe''. April 14, 2009. Retrieved April 29, 2010.</ref>

===Bangladesh===
Population censuses were conducted by the [[Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics]] (BBS) in 1974, 1981, 1991, 2001, 2011 and 2022. The 2022 Census was the nation's first digital census.{{citation needed|date=November 2023}}

===China===
{{main|Census in China}}
{{see also|Population history of China}}

From [[Xinhai Revolution|the end]] of the [[Imperial China|imperial period]] in 1911, China's first censuses were irregular: the [[Republic of China (1912–1949)|Republic of China]] held censuses in 1913 and 1944. Under [[Mao Zedong]], the People's Republic of China held its first in [[1952 Chinese Census|1952]], but the second in [[1963 Chinese Census|1963]] was secret and unacknowledged until the early 1980s.

The [[1982 Chinese census]] was much more thorough and well-conducted than the first two, and similar censuses have been conducted decennially in 1990, 2000, [[2010 Chinese census|2010]], and 2020.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stats.gov.cn/tjgb/rkpcgb/index.htm |script-title=zh:中华人民共和国国家统计局 >> 人口普查公报 |publisher=Stats.gov.cn |access-date=2010-11-30 |language=zh |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110309025915/http://www.stats.gov.cn/tjgb/rkpcgb/index.htm |archive-date=March 9, 2011 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> These are the world's biggest censuses and over 6 million enumerators were engaged in the 2000{{citation needed|date=October 2011}} and 2010 censuses.

Between the national censuses, 1% National Population Sample Surveys were taken in 1987, 1995, and 2005; 0.1% National Population Sample Surveys have been taken annually since 2000.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stats.gov.cn/tjdt/gjtjjdt/t20091221_402608717.htm |title=李克强主持召开人口普查领导小组会议时强调 把握我国基本国情 促进可持续发展 |publisher=Stats.gov.cn |date=December 21, 2009 |access-date=2010-11-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401234648/http://www.stats.gov.cn/tjdt/gjtjjdt/t20091221_402608717.htm |archive-date=April 1, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref> National agricultural, economic, and industrial censuses are also taken on a regular basis. The first economic census was taken in 2004 and the second 2008.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stats.gov.cn/was40/gjtjj_en_detail.jsp?channelid=4920&record=1 |title=Communiqué on Major Data of the Second National Economic Census (No.1) |publisher=Stats.gov.cn |date=December 25, 2009 |access-date=2010-11-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120401234701/http://www.stats.gov.cn/was40/gjtjj_en_detail.jsp?channelid=4920&record=1 |archive-date=April 1, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Cyprus===
{{unreferenced section|date=November 2013}}

The British carried out seven censuses in [[Cyprus]] in total: six at ten-year intervals between 1881 and 1931, and the last in 1946. Following the establishment of the modern state, there have been seven more censuses: in 1960 (the year of establishment), 1973, 1976, 1982, 1992, 2001 and 2011. The Statistical Service of the Cypriot government counts from the first British census, i.e. the latest census, in 2011, is referred to as the 14th census. In [[Northern Cyprus]] there have been three censuses: in 1996, 2006 and 2011. All three have been a matter of controversy, both in the north and the south, and abroad.

===Hong Kong===
{{Main|Population Census in Hong Kong}}

Census takes place every [[decennial|10 years]] and by-census between two censuses by the [[Census and Statistics Department]] of [[Government of Hong Kong|Hong Kong]]. The last census was the [[2021 Population Census in Hong Kong]].

===India===
<!-- This section is linked from [[Parsi]] -->
{{Main|Census of India}}

The decennial census of India is the primary source of information about the demographic characteristics of the [[population of India]]. The 2011 census is one of the largest censuses in the history of mankind.<ref name="dnaindia.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.dnaindia.com/india/report_census-2011-kicks-off-today_1366020 |title=Census-2011 kicks off today – India – DNA |publisher=Dnaindia.com |date=April 1, 2010 |access-date=2010-11-30}}</ref>

The first census in India in modern times was conducted in 1873. First regular census was started in 1881 by [[George Robinson, 1st Marquess of Ripon|Lord Ripon]]. Since then, a population census has been carried out every [[decennial|10 years]]. The [[15th Indian national census|latest census]] commenced on May 1, 2010. It will create a [[National Population Register]] with photographs and fingerprints of every resident. All usual residents of India will also be provided with their Unique ID numbers and [[National Identity Card]]s.
The census is carried out by the office of the [[Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India]], Delhi, an office in the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India, under the 1948 Census of India Act. The act gives Central Government many powers like to notify a date for Census, power to ask for the services of any citizen for census work. The law makes it compulsory for every citizen to answer the census questions truthfully. The Act provides penalties for giving false answers or not giving answers at all to the census questionnaire. One of the most important provisions of law is the guarantee for the maintenance of secrecy of the information collected at the census of each individual. The census records are not open to inspection and also not admissible in evidence.

The census is conducted in two phases: first, house listing and [[house numbering]] phase and second, the actual population enumeration phase. The census is carried out by the canvassing method. In this method, each household is visited and the information is collected by specially trained enumerator. They collect data related to households e.g. number of members, water & electricity supply, ownership of land, vehicles, computers and other assets and services. In the second phase, total population is counted and statistics related to individuals are collected and saved into the governments hand.<ref name="dnaindia.com"/>

===Indonesia===
The first population census was done during the colonial era, 1930. Before that, a non-overall census was already conducted in 1920. After that census was done irregularly. The first census after independence was 1961, followed by 1971. Since 1980 it is conducted regularly every 10 years. In between, there is also economical census (every 10 years, five years after population census) and agricultural census (three years after population census). The last census was held in September 2020 ([[2020 Indonesian census]]).

===Iran===
{{Main|Demographics of Iran}}

The Statistical Center of Iran carries out nationwide population and housing censuses every ten years, the first of which conducted in 1956 (1335 [[Iranian calendar|AP]]) reporting a total population of 19 million people. Since then, seven other censuses were conducted in 1966, 1976, 1986, 1996, 2006, 2011, 2016. As seen, the two censuses in 2006 and 2011 were conducted on a five-year basis, following a 2008 law. The law was rescinded in 2020, with the president announcing that the next census would be conducted in 2026, due to modernizing method to Register-based Census.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-05-13|title=سرشماری عمومی نفوس و مسکن، سال ۱۴۰۵ برگزار می‌شود|url=https://www.irna.ir/news/83786591/سرشماری-عمومی-نفوس-و-مسکن-سال-۱۴۰۵-برگزار-می-شود|access-date=2020-11-22|website=ایرنا|language=fa}}</ref>

===Iraq===
{{Main|Demographics of Iraq}}

The Central Statistical Organization – Ministry of Planning of Iraq is responsible for population and housing censuses.

According to the British government in Iraq, the population estimate in 1920 was 3 million. In 1927, the General Directorate of Population carried out the census, the population estimate was 2,968,054. Later, there were another 8 censuses in the years 1934, 1947, 1957, 1965, 1977, 1987, 1997 and the last one that was carried out in 2024.

The 1997 census was considered to be incomplete as the Kurdistan region was not counted at the census.

After the [[War of Iraq]], there was a plan for a new population and housing census, and in November 2024 the first nationwide census in nearly 40 years, however the ethnicity question was 
omitted due to conflicts. The 2024 census counted that 45.4 million people lived in Iraq <ref>{{cite web | title=Iraq's population grew to 45.4 million according to the first survey in decades | website=[[Associated Press News]] | date=November 25, 2024 | url=https://apnews.com/article/iraq-population-census-a74ca47e45036b9a593824df0d5889e3 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Iraq to hold first nationwide census since 1987 | work=Reuters | date=November 19, 2024 | url=https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/iraq-hold-first-nationwide-census-since-1987-2024-11-19/ }}</ref>

===Israel===
The first census in the state of Israel was held in November 1948, six months after its creation, to establish the [[population registry]].<ref name="isr1">{{cite web|url=http://www.cbs.gov.il/mifkad/census2008_e.pdf|title=The 2008 Israel Integrated Census of Population and Housing: Basic conception and procedure|last=Kamen|first=Charles S.|date=February 2005|publisher=Israel Central Bureau of Statistics|access-date=2008-10-12|page=1|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081028203850/http://www.cbs.gov.il/mifkad/census2008_e.pdf|archive-date=October 28, 2008|url-status=dead}}</ref> Subsequent censuses were conducted by the [[Israel Central Bureau of Statistics]] (ICBS) in 1961, 1972, 1983, 1995 and 2008.<ref name="isr1"/> In these, 20% of households completed a detailed survey and the remainder a shorter questionnaire.<ref name="isr1"/> There is no legal requirement to hold a census within a given interval; in practice, the ICBS requests and the government decides.<ref name="isr1"/> The next census is scheduled for 2022.<ref>[http://www.cbs.gov.il/census/census/main_mifkad08.html Main Mifkad] cbs.gov.il {{in lang|he}} {{dead link|date=September 2023}}</ref>

===Japan===
{{Main|Demographics of Japan}}

Since 1920, Japan has conducted {{ill| Population Census (Japan)|ja|国勢調査 (日本) |lt= Population Census }} to collect census information every five years,<ref name="stat.go.jp">{{Cite web|url=https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/kokusei/index.html|title=Population Census | website= Statistics Bureau of Japan}}</ref> with the exceptions of the 6th in 1947 instead of 1945 and some extra censuses during 1944–1948.<ref name=Japan_outline_2020>{{Cite web 
| url=https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/kokusei/2020/pdf/outline.pdf
| title = Outline of the 2020 Population Census of Japan
| date = 2020
| publisher = Statistics Bureau of Japan
| id = {{URL|https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/kokusei/}}
| accessdate = 2024-06-04
}}</ref> A large-scale census (in the years ending in the digit 0) and a simplified one (in those ending in 5) has been undertaken alternately. They collected information as of October 1.<ref>{{cite web
 |title       = Population Census 2010
 |publisher   = Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
 |url         = http://www.stat.go.jp/data/kokusei/2010/special/english/index.htm
 |year        = 2010
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20121115193524/http://www.stat.go.jp/data//kokusei/2010/special/english/index.htm
 |archive-date = November 15, 2012
 |df          = mdy-all
}}</ref> The [[Statistics Bureau (Japan)|Statistics Bureau]] is in charge of the exercise of censuses.<ref name="stat.go.jp"/>

The questionnaires were frequently changed in the early history of the Population Census, but they were almost fixed by the 1970s.<ref name=Sato_2015>{{Cite book |language=ja| author = 佐藤正広| title = 国勢調査: 日本社会の百年| publisher = 岩波書店| date = 2015| series = 岩波現代全書 | isbn = 9784000291613 }}</ref>{{Rp|page=148}} Since then, they include 16–23 topics, with a small difference between the large-scale censuses and the simplified ones.<ref name=Japan_guide_2020>{{Cite book| language=ja | url=https://www.stat.go.jp/data/kokusei/2020/kekka/pdf/u_guide_2020.pdf|title=令和２年国勢調査調査結果の利用案内: ユーザーズガイド| date= 2021| accessdate = 2024-06-04| author = Statistics Bureau of Japan | publisher=総務省統計局 |id = {{URL|https://id.ndl.go.jp/bib/031391709}}}}</ref>{{Rp|page=135}} They solicit information such as name, gender, relationship to head of household, year and month of birth, marital status, nationality, number of the household members, type and tenure of dwelling, floor area of the dwelling, number of hours worked during the week prior to October 1, employment status, name of employer and type of business, kind of work, and the place of work or schooling.<ref name=Japan_outline_2015>{{Cite web 
| url=https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/kokusei/2015/pdf/outline.pdf
| title = Outline of the 2015 Population Census of Japan
| date = 2015
| publisher = Statistics Bureau of Japan
| id = {{URL|https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/kokusei/}}
| accessdate = 2024-06-04
}}</ref>  For the years ending in the digit 0, the questionnaire includes additional questions such as education, how long the respondent has lived at the current address, the place he/she lived five years ago, and the means of transportation to the workplace or school.<ref name=Japan_q_2020>{{Cite web | url=https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/kokusei/2020/pdf/qre.pdf
| author =
| title = Questionnaire (2020 Population Census)
| date = 2020
| publisher = Statistics Bureau of Japan
| id = {{URL|https://www.stat.go.jp/english/data/kokusei/}}
| accessdate = 2024-06-04
}}</ref>

Regardless of nationality or legal status, all residents in Japan are required to complete the census. All information collected by the census is confidential and protected by the {{ill|Statistics Act (Japan)|ja|統計法| lt=Statistics Act}}. Information provided by census can never be used for any investigation purposes such as immigration control, police investigation, tax collections and so on.<ref name="jp.2020.en">{{cite web |url=https://www.kokusei2020.go.jp/en/index.html |title=Census 2020 |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Census 2020 |publisher=Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications |access-date=2020-09-14 |archive-date=September 3, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200903130333/https://www.kokusei2020.go.jp/en/index.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> After the census, all forms are destroyed.

For the first time in 2010, residents of Tokyo were given an option to complete the census questionnaires online in lieu of the conventional paper questionnaires. Unique ID and password were provided with the census form. Tokyo was chosen as the initial rollout for the online questionnaires due to the high concentration of people living in [[apartment buildings]] or [[gated communities]], which restricts the access of census workers. The online options were made available across Japan from the 2015 census.

The 2020 census was conducted in midst of global [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and the Japanese government urged the residents to respond the census online. Those who are unable to respond online may complete and mail back the paper questionnaires.<ref name="jp.2020.en" /> The online census questionnaires are available in Japanese, English, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, Korean, Vietnamese, Spanish, and Portuguese.<ref name="jp.2020.en" /> The paper census form was only written in Japanese, but translation was available in 29 different languages upon request.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.kokusei2020.go.jp/household/language.html |title=Language support |author=<!--Not stated--> |website=Census 2020 |publisher=Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications |access-date=2020-09-14 |archive-date=September 16, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200916062939/https://www.kokusei2020.go.jp/household/language.html |url-status=dead }}</ref> Since 2020, administrative information can be used on limited basis, only to complete the number of persons from nonresponding households.<ref name=Yomiuri_20201022>{{Cite news| language=ja
| url=https://www.yomiuri.co.jp/politics/20201022-OYT1T50018/
| title = 国勢調査、住基情報の転用可能に…非回答の世帯対象
| newspaper = 読売新聞オンライン
| date =  2020-10-22
| publisher = Yomiuri Shimbun
| accessdate = 2024-06-04
}}</ref>

===Jordan===
{{unreferenced section|date=October 2025}}
The first population census after Jordanian independence in 1946 was taken in 1952. It only counted the number of people in households, and could therefore be considered only to be a housing census. The first complete census was taken in 1961, with further censuses taken in 1979, 1994, 2004 and 2015. The distribution of [[Palestinians]] and [[Jordanians]] within the population has been a politically sensitive issue since the [[Six-Day war]] in 1967.

===Lebanon===
No census has been conducted in [[Lebanon]] since 1932.<ref name="AJECensus">{{cite news|last=al-Issawi|first= Omar |date=June 4, 2009|url=http://english.aljazeera.net/focus/2009/05/2009527115531294628.html |title=Lebanon's Palestinian refugees|work= [[Al Jazeera English|Al Jazeera]]}}</ref> It indicated a population of 861,399 Lebanese.<ref>Rolland, John C. (2003). ''Lebanon: current issues and background.'' Nova Publishers. p. 65.</ref> Various estimates of the population have been taken since; in 1956 it was estimated a population of 1,411,416, with 54% Christian and 44% Muslim. Conducting a census since then has been complicated by various conflicts in the 1970s and 1980s,<ref>[https://countrystudies.us/lebanon/34.htm Lebanon]. Country studies.</ref> as well as by the sensitivity of religious issues.<ref name="AJECensus" />

===Malaysia===
{{main|Census in Malaysia}}

The census in [[Malaysia]] is carried out every 10 years, like many nations, since 1960 (with the exception of the fourth census, which was carried out in 1991). The next census should be carried out in 2030. The most recent census was from July 7 to October 24, 2020.

===Myanmar===
{{main|Census in Myanmar}}

A general census of population and housing has been conducted in years 1973, 1983, 2014 and 2024 with the 2024 Census data considered unreliable with a provisional count of 51.3 million. A decrease from 51.5 Million, with prelimeneary census being published in December 2024.<ref>{{cite web | last1=Naing | first1=Shoon | title=Myanmar says 2024 census shows population of 51.3 million | work=Reuters | date=January 2025 | url=https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/myanmar-says-2024-census-shows-population-513-mln-2025-01-01/ }}</ref>

===Nepal===
{{main|Census in Nepal}}

Census in [[Nepal]] are taken by [[Central Bureau of Statistics (Nepal)|Central Bureau of Statistics]]. Population censuses are conducted every ten years in [[Nepal]]. The first was held in 1911 and the most recent was held in [[2021 Nepal census|2021]]. The census in 2021 is the first census of [[Nepal|Federal Nepal]].

===Oman===
Censuses have been taken in the [[Sultanate of Oman]] in 1993, 2003, 2010 and 2020.

===Philippines===
{{Main|Census in the Philippines}}

The census of the [[Philippines]] is enumerated every 5 years (beginning in 1960, except in 2005 where it was moved to 2007 due to budgetary constraints) and the results are used to allocate Congressional seats (congressional apportionment) and government program funding.

The census is performed by the [[Philippine Statistics Authority]]. The first official census in the Philippines was carried out by the Spanish government pursuant to a royal decree calling for the counting of persons living as of the midnight of December 31, 1877. The first door-to-door census was conducted in 1903 to fulfill Public Act 467 which was approved by the U.S. Congress in July 1902. The last national census was held in 2020. For years between the censuses, the PSA issues estimates made using surveys and statistical models.

===Saudi Arabia===
Population censuses have been taken in Saudi Arabia in 1962/63 (incomplete), 1974 (complete but not reliable), 1992, 2004, 2010 and 2022. An agriculture census was taken in 1999 and 2015.

===Singapore===
Population censuses have been taken in Singapore every ten years, in 1970, 1980, 1990, 2000, 2010 and 2020.

===South Korea===
South Korea had its first "modern" census in 1925.<ref>{{Cite web|title=2020 인구주택총조사|url=https://www.census.go.kr/cui/cuiKorView.do?q_menu=3&q_sub=3|access-date=2022-01-23|website=Census Korea|language=ko}}</ref>

The Census has been conducted 18 times every 5 years, most recently in 2020.

===Sri Lanka===
{{Main|Census of Sri Lanka}}
The census in Sri Lanka is carried out by the Department of Census and Statistics every [[decennial|10 years]], with the next one being planned for 2033.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://archives.sundayobserver.lk/2010/05/16/new30.asp |title=Sri Lanka News |publisher=Sundayobserver.lk |date=May 16, 2010 |access-date=2010-11-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121120215803/http://www.sundayobserver.lk/2010/05/16/new30.asp |archive-date=November 20, 2012 |url-status=live }}</ref> The 2011 one being the first post-war census in three decades. The census will cover all [[Grama Niladhari]] (GN) divisions of the country. The first scientific census in Sri Lanka was conducted on March 27, 1871. The last four were in 1963, 1971, 1981, 2001, 2012 and 2024 with a census estimate in 1989. The 2001 census was only carried out in 18 [[Districts of Sri Lanka|Districts]] due to the [[Sri Lankan civil war|Sri Lankan Civil War]].

===Syria===
The first population census in Syria was taken by the French Mandatory Regime in 1921–22. This is however not considered reliable. Censuses during independence have been taken 1947, 1960 (the first comprehensive demographic investigation), 1970, 1976 (a sample census), 1981, 1994 and 2004 and the next would be taken at 2017.

===Taiwan===
The first census in [[Taiwan]] was conducted in 1905, while [[Taiwan under Japanese rule|Taiwan was under Japanese rule]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ind.org.tw/LIT_13/20010312.pdf|title=The Modernization of Taiwan|access-date=November 14, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425015246/http://www.ind.org.tw/LIT_13/20010312.pdf|archive-date=April 25, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Thailand===
A census is conducted every 10 years, the latest being in 2020. The [[National Statistical Office of Thailand]] is in charge of conducting the census.

===Turkey===
{{main|Census in Turkey}}

The Turkish census is run by the [[Turkish Statistical Institute]]. The first census in [[Turkey]] was conducted in 1927. After 1935, it took place every 5 years until 1990. Now, the census takes place every 10 years. The last census was in 2000. It can be noted that the census enumeration takes place on one single day in Turkey (in other countries it takes 1–2 weeks). This required some 900,000 enumerators in 2000. The 15th census based on improved geographical information systems is planned for 2010.

A census was taken in the [[Ottoman Empire]] 1831–38 by [[Sultan Mahmud II]] (1808–1839) as a part of the reform movement [[Tanzimat]]. Christian and Jewish men were counted but the female population was excluded.

===Uzbekistan===
The last census in Uzbekistan was carried out in 1989 during Soviet rule. Uzbekistan itself will carry out their first post-Soviet census either in 2025 or 2026.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.gazeta.uz/en/2024/03/17/population-census/ |title=Population census in Uzbekistan is now scheduled for 2025−2026 |date=March 17, 2024 |website=Gazeta.uz |access-date=March 16, 2025}}</ref>

==Europe==
===Albania===
{{main|Census in Albania}}

The latest population census was conducted in Albania on September 18, 2023.

The previous census was conducted in September 2011.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.instat.gov.al/media/177354/main_results__population_and_housing_census_2011.pdf |title=Population and Housing Census 2011, 2011 |access-date=2013-09-03 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141114073838/http://www.instat.gov.al/media/177354/main_results__population_and_housing_census_2011.pdf |archive-date=November 14, 2014 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> Prior to that, censuses were conducted in April 2001 and in 1989 at the end of the [[Communist Albania|Communist regime]].

Since 1968, the population number is permanently up to date through the [[National Register (Belgium)|National Register]].

===Bosnia and Herzegovina===
Population censuses in Bosnia and Herzegovina were conducted in 1879, 1885, 1895, 1910, 1921, 1931, 1948, [[1953 population census in Bosnia and Herzegovina|1953]], 1961, 1971, 1981 and [[1991 population census in Bosnia and Herzegovina|1991]]. The [[2013 population census in Bosnia and Herzegovina|2013 Census]] was organized in period between October 1–15, 2013. This is the first census after the end of the [[Bosnian War]].

===Bulgaria===
Bulgarian governors organized a national census soon after the liberation of the Bulgarian lands. In 1881 a census took place in
the Principality, while in 1884 a census was organized in [[Eastern Rumelia]]. The first census covering the unified state took place in 1887.

Since these first accounts, Bulgarian authorities had organized several population censuses: 1892, 1900, 1905, 1910, 1920, 1926, 1934, 1946, 1956, 1965, 1975, 1985, 1992, 2001, and 2011.

The data provided in the Bulgarian censuses from 1888 until [[World War II]] is regarded as highly reliable{{Citation needed|date=February 2011}} according to the standards of the time. The Bulgarian leading statisticians of the period were generally educated in Western universities and participated vividly in the international cooperation, therefore insisted and succeeded in introducing the best practices of the time. The quality of the data provided of later censuses is a matter of debate.{{Citation needed|date=February 2011}} The religion question in the 2001 census didn't allow the unaffiliated Bulgarians to be counted as such.

===Croatia===
The census in [[Croatia]] is carried out every 10 years. The last census was taken in 2021 with final population count of 3.9 million.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://dzs.gov.hr/vijesti/objavljeni-konacni-rezultati-popisa-2021/1270 | title=Objavljeni konačni rezultati Popisa 2021 }}</ref> The first census was in 1857 when what is now [[Croatia]] was part of the [[Austrian Empire]].

===Czech Republic===
The census in the [[Czech Republic]] is carried out every 10 years by the Czech Statistical Office. The last census was taken in 2021. Earlier censuses were taken in 1869, 1880, 1890, 1900, 1910, 1921, 1930, 1950, 1961, 1970, 1980, 1991, 2001 and 2011.

The results of the last census are also available via the interactive model based software.

===Denmark===
The first Danish census was in 1700–1701, and contained statistical information about adult men. Only about half of it still exists. A census of school children was taken during the 1730s.

Following these early undertakings, the first census to attempt completely covering all citizens (including women and children who had previously been listed only as numbers) of [[Denmark-Norway]] was taken in 1769.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.rhd.uit.no/census/ft1769.html|title=Census 1769|access-date=November 14, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120722230700/http://www.rhd.uit.no/census/ft1769.html|archive-date=July 22, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> At that point there were 797,584 citizens in the kingdom. [[Georg Christian Oeder]] took a statistical census in 1771 which covered [[Copenhagen]], [[Sjælland]], [[Møn]], and [[Bornholm]].

After that, censuses followed somewhat regularly in 1787, 1801, and 1834, and between 1840 and 1860, the censuses were taken every five years, and then every ten years until 1890. Special censuses for Copenhagen were taken in 1885 and 1895.

In the 20th century, censuses were taken every five years from 1901 to 1921, and then every ten years from 1930. The last traditional census was taken in 1970.

A limited population census based on registers was taken in 1976. From 1981 and each year onwards information that corresponds to a population and housing census is retrieved from registers. Denmark was the first country in the world to conduct these censuses from administrative registers. The most important registers are the Population Register ([[Det Centrale Personregister]]), the Building and Dwelling Register ([[Bygnings- og Boligregistret]]) and the Enterprise Register ([[Det Centrale Virksomhedsregister]]). The central statistical office, [[Statistics Denmark]] is responsible for compiling these data. This information is available online in the Statbank Denmark.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.statbank.dk |title=Statbank Denmark |publisher=Statbank.dk |access-date=2010-11-30}}</ref>

It is possible to search a portion of the Danish censuses online at the Dansk Demografisk Database,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ddd.dda.dk/ |title=Dansk Demografisk Database |publisher=Ddd.dda.dk |access-date=2010-11-30}}</ref> and also view scanned versions at Arkivalier Online.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.arkivalieronline.dk/ |title=Arkivalier Online |publisher=Arkivalieronline.dk |access-date=2010-11-30}}</ref>

===Estonia===
Population censuses have been carried out in 1881,<ref name="stat.ee">{{cite web|url=http://www.stat.ee/26384|title=General data for 1881, 1897, 1922, 1934, 1959, 1970, 1979, 1989 censuses – Statistics Estonia|website=www.stat.ee|access-date=December 4, 2014|archive-date=June 4, 2012|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120604233416/http://www.stat.ee/26384|url-status=dead}}</ref> 1897,<ref name="stat.ee"/> 1922,<ref name="stat.ee"/> 1934,<ref name="stat.ee"/> 1959,<ref name="stat.ee1">{{cite web|url=http://www.stat.ee/26332|title=Publications of the results of the 1959, 1970, 1979, 1989 censuses – Statistics Estonia|website=www.stat.ee|access-date=December 4, 2014|archive-date=December 7, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207045237/http://www.stat.ee/26332|url-status=dead}}</ref> 1970,<ref name="stat.ee1"/> 1979,<ref name="stat.ee1"/> 1989,<ref name="stat.ee1"/> 2000<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stat.ee/population-census-2000|title=2000 Population and Housing Census – Statistics Estonia|website=www.stat.ee|access-date=December 4, 2014|archive-date=December 7, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207053509/http://www.stat.ee/population-census-2000|url-status=dead}}</ref> and 2011.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stat.ee/59344|title=REL2011 – Rahvaloendus käivitus hoogsalt|website=www.stat.ee|access-date=November 14, 2012|archive-date=November 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121113181911/http://www.stat.ee/59344|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stat.ee/26383|title=Population censuses in Estonia – Statistics Estonia|website=www.stat.ee|access-date=November 14, 2012|archive-date=October 29, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029184031/http://www.stat.ee/26383|url-status=dead}}</ref>

The censuses of 1881 and 1897 were carried out during the reign of the [[Russian Empire]], when Estonia was divided between the [[Governorate of Estonia]] and the [[Governorate of Livonia]]. The latter also included territories of modern-day Latvia, however its Estonian-populated counties of [[Kreis Werro|Võru]], [[Kreis Dorpat|Tartu]], [[Kreis Fellin|Viljandi]], [[Kreis Pernau|Pärnu]] and [[Kreis Ösel|Saaremaa]] roughly corresponded to the later borders of the Republic of Estonia. Only later Estonian territories of [[Valga, Estonia|Valga]], [[Narva]], [[Ivangorod|Jaanilinn]] and [[Petseri County]] remained outside these figures.

The 1922 and 1934 censuses were carried out by the independent Republic of Estonia. The 1959, 1979 and 1989 censuses were carried out by the [[Estonian SSR]] of the [[Soviet Union]] and excluded Jaanilinn and Petseri County, which were annexed by the [[Russian SFSR]] in 1945. The 2000 and 2011 censuses were again carried out by the independent Republic of Estonia and also excluded the territories annexed by Russia in 1945. The current responsible institution is the [[Statistics Estonia]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.stat.ee/censuses |title=Statistics Estonia |publisher=Stat.ee |date=July 19, 2010 |access-date=2010-11-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121113155955/http://www.stat.ee/censuses |archive-date=November 13, 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Finland===
The first population census was taken in 1749 when Finland was a part of Sweden. Although the parliament authorized a modern census in 1938, it was not undertaken until 1950. Finland has an accurate population registry system, thus censuses are in practice conducted by studying the registry, rather than as a separate project. Statistics Finland publishes various statistics on population: preliminary population statistics are published monthly, population structure report is published annually and population projections every three years. Once in ten years, the official locations and demarcations for densely populated areas (taajama) for traffic purposes, and official numbers of the speakers of national languages (Finnish or Swedish), for bilinguality, are reviewed.

===France===
The census in France is currently carried out by [[INSEE]]. The first census in France was conducted in 1801.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ined.fr/fichier/t_publication/532/publi_pdf2_pop.and.soc.english.409.pdf|title = Counting the population}}</ref> Since 2004, a partial census has been carried out every year, and the results published as averages over 5 years.

===Germany===
{{Main|Census in Germany}}

{{Update|section|inaccurate=yes|date=October 2012}}
The first systematic population on the European continent was taken in 1719 in [[Prussia]] (roughly corresponding to today's northern Germany and western Poland).

The first large-scale census in the German Empire took place in [[German census of 1895|1895]]. Attempts at introducing a census in [[West Germany]] sparked strong popular resentment in the 1980s since many quite personal questions were asked. Some campaigned for a boycott. In the end the [[Constitutional Court of Germany|Constitutional Court]] stopped the census in 1980 and 1983. The last census of West Germany was in 1987. Germany has since used [[Sampling (statistics)|population samples]] in combination with statistical methods, in place of a full census. But finally, on May 9, 2011, a new census of Germany was completed.

===Greece===
{{main|Census in Greece}}

Census takes place every [[decennial|10 years]] and is carried out by the National Statistical Service of Greece.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.statistics.gr/|title=Κεντρική Σελίδα ΕΛΣΤΑΤ|website=www.statistics.gr|access-date=November 14, 2012|archive-date=February 27, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110227225934/http://www.statistics.gr/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The 2011 census ended on 24 May.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.apografi2011.gr/en/index.php |title=Census 2011 |publisher=Apografi2011.gr |access-date=2012-02-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110902081539/http://www.apografi2011.gr/en/index.php |archive-date=September 2, 2011 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

===Hungary===
Official decennial censuses have been taken in Hungary since 1870; the latest one – in line with the recommendations of the United Nations and the Statistical Office of the European Union – was carried out in 2011.
Starting from 1880 the Hungarian census system was based on native language (the language spoken at home in the early life of the person and at the time of the survey), vulgar language (the most frequently used language in the family), and other spoken languages.

===Iceland===
The first Icelandic census took place in [[Icelandic census of 1703|1703]], following upon the first Danish census of 1700–1701. Further censuses were carried out in 1801, 1845 and 1865. The 1703 exercise was the first census ever to cover all inhabitants of an entire country, mentioning the name, age, and social position of each individual. All of the information still exists, although some of the original documents have been lost.

The need for censuses was eliminated through the setting up, in 1952, of the National Registry (''Þjóðskrá''), which later merged with other entities to form [[Registers Iceland]]. All those born in Iceland, and all new residents, are automatically registered. Individuals are identified in the registry by means of a [[national identification number]] (the so-called ''[[kennitala]]''), a number composed of the date of birth in the format {{mono|ddmmyy}} and four additional digits, the third of which is a control digit, and the last of which indicates the century in which the person was born (9 for the 1900s and 0 for the 2000s).

The National Registry doubles as an [[electoral register]]. Likewise, all bank accounts are linked to the national identification of the owner (companies and institutions all have their own identification numbers).

===Ireland===
{{Main|2022 census of Ireland}}

Population censuses covering all of Ireland were conducted every ten years from 1821 to 1911 inclusive. The first census following independence was conducted in 1926 and done every ten years until 1946. Since then, most censuses have been conducted every five years from 1951 to 2011 with two exceptions. Instead of censuses in 1976 and 2001, they were instead conducted in 1979 and 2002 respectively. The next census is scheduled for 2022, having been postponed from 2021 due to the COVID-19 pandemic.<ref>{{citation|url= https://www.cso.ie/en/csolatestnews/pressreleases/2020pressreleases/pressstatementpostponementofcensus2021/|title=Postponement of Census 2021}}</ref> All original census returns from 1901 onwards survive, together with some 19th century fragments.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/help/history.html|title=History of Irish Census Records|publisher=National Archives of Ireland|access-date=2015-07-17}}</ref>

The census in Ireland is carried out by the [[Central Statistics Office (Ireland)|Central Statistics Office]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cso.ie/census/default.htm|title=CSO Census Home Page|access-date=2008-10-09}}</ref> The census is taken every five years, with more detailed information collected in years ending in 1 and less in the years ending in 6. The 1976 census was cancelled as a cost-saving measure, but a supplementary census was held in 1979 after it became apparent that the 1970s had seen major demographic changes.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.irisheu-silc.net/census/Historical_Perspective.htm |title=Census: Historical perspective |publisher=CSO |access-date=2008-10-09 }}{{dead link|date=May 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> The census scheduled for 2001 was postponed until 2002 due to [[2001 United Kingdom foot-and-mouth outbreak|the outbreak of foot-and-mouth disease]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cso.ie/census/Commentary.htm|title=Census 2002 Results |year=2002|publisher=CSO|access-date=2008-10-09 |quote=The census originally planned for 29 April 2001 was postponed because of the Foot and Mouth disease situation pertaining at the time.}}</ref>

Data from the 1901 Census of Ireland and the [[1911 census of Ireland]] were first made publicly available in 1961.<ref name="oldrecords">{{cite web|url=https://www.cso.ie/census/Access_to_Records.htm|title=Access to old records|publisher=CSO|access-date=2008-10-09}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/|title=Census of Ireland, Dublin 1911|publisher=National Archives of Ireland|access-date=2008-10-09}}</ref> Subsequent census records will be made available 100 years after collection.<ref name="oldrecords"/> The 1901 and 1911 census returns, together with the 19th century fragments, are freely available to view at the National Archives of Ireland website.<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.census.nationalarchives.ie/search/.html|title=Census Search|publisher=National Archives of Ireland|access-date=2015-07-17}}{{Dead link|date=May 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

===Italy===
The census in Italy is carried out by [[Istituto Nazionale di Statistica|ISTAT]] every [[decennial|10 years]]. The last five were in 1971, 1981, 1991, 2001 and 2011.
From 2018, the census will be done every year, using a sample of population to correct databases that ISTAT create from registry offices and other public offices.
